world.title: Carney says Washington must meet Canadian terms for tariff deal
world.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday that U.S.-Canada trade talks had intensified slightly, but any progress reflected Washington moving toward Ottawa’s demands, not a change in Canada’s position. His comments came eight days before U.S. midterm elections, as President Donald Trump and White House economic a
world.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday that U.S.-Canada trade talks had intensified slightly, but any progress reflected Washington moving toward Ottawa’s demands, not a change in Canada’s position. His comments came eight days before U.S. midterm elections, as President Donald Trump and White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett described a deal as close. Canadian officials and people familiar with the talks, however, said negotiations remained uncertain: no formal negotiating documents had been exchanged, and any agreement could be limited to specific industries. The standoff followed the collapse of talks in August, when Carney said U.S. demands crossed Canadian “red lines.” Trump then imposed tariffs of up to 50% on about $20 billion of Canadian goods, and Canada retaliated. On Oct. 23, Trump announced exemptions for some Canadian imports while adding tariffs to other products. The duties have become an issue in competitive U.S. Senate races. Reporting on the negotiations points to possible relief on steel and autos rather than a settlement of the broader trade dispute. Carney said he could not be sure Washington would honor a future agreement. U.S. officials have publicly predicted a deal but have not confirmed an agreement. The U.S. midterms are Nov. 3; Carney is also due to host European Union leaders in Montreal on Oct. 29-30 to discuss closer economic and security ties.

world.title: UN inquiry says Israel continued genocidal acts in Gaza after ceasefire
world.summary: A United Nations commission of inquiry said Israel continued to commit genocidal acts in Gaza after the U.S.-brokered ceasefire began in October 2025, and accused Israeli forces of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the occupied West Bank. Israel rejected the report as a misinformation campaign and denied the ac
world.content: A United Nations commission of inquiry said Israel continued to commit genocidal acts in Gaza after the U.S.-brokered ceasefire began in October 2025, and accused Israeli forces of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the occupied West Bank. Israel rejected the report as a misinformation campaign and denied the accusations. The commission said Israeli forces continued using heavy weapons, drones, artillery and sniper fire in populated areas during the truce. It described the Yellow Line, which initially marked the ceasefire boundary, as an advancing de facto border as Israeli-controlled territory expanded from 53% to at least 60% of Gaza. It attributed at least 196 Palestinian deaths to fire along the expanding front. The report also alleged extermination, persecution, torture and sexual violence in the West Bank, and said the Palestinian Authority had targeted people expressing dissent. Israel rejected the findings as Israelis voted in a general election on Oct. 27.
world.image_alt: UN inquiry says Israel continued genocidal acts in Gaza after ceasefire

world.title: Pope Leo cleared to visit three South American countries after cancer surgery
world.summary: The Vatican said Monday that Pope Leo XIV will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on Nov. 6-17 as planned after medical tests found no medical reason to cancel the trip following lung cancer surgery. Surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung on Oct. 13; subsequent examinations found the adenocarcinoma was locali
world.content: The Vatican said Monday that Pope Leo XIV will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on Nov. 6-17 as planned after medical tests found no medical reason to cancel the trip following lung cancer surgery. Surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung on Oct. 13; subsequent examinations found the adenocarcinoma was localized, and the Vatican said he does not need further cancer treatment. The 10-city journey includes 14 flights and two helicopter trips, covers about 31,000 kilometers and includes a stop in Cuzco, Peru, at roughly 3,300 meters above sea level. The Vatican said the itinerary will not change despite the travel demands and the high-altitude visit. Leo has gradually resumed public duties on a schedule adjusted to allow for rest. He appeared at the Angelus prayer on Oct. 25 but canceled an Oct. 27 visit to Assisi on medical advice. That visit would have required a helicopter flight. His South American itinerary is due to begin in Uruguay on Nov. 6.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo cleared to visit three South American countries after cancer surgery

world.title: Machado offers talks as U.S. outlines route to Venezuelan elections
world.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado said Monday she was willing to meet interim President Delcy Rodríguez after returning from nearly 10 months in exile, while pressing for a presidential election in 2027. Machado’s movement remains outside U.S.-backed negotiations between Rodríguez’s government and anoth
world.content: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado said Monday she was willing to meet interim President Delcy Rodríguez after returning from nearly 10 months in exile, while pressing for a presidential election in 2027. Machado’s movement remains outside U.S.-backed negotiations between Rodríguez’s government and another opposition faction. U.S. officials outlined a transition plan: overhaul the Supreme Court and electoral council, then have Rodríguez declare the presidency vacant, triggering a constitutional six-month period to hold an election. The vote would likely fall in 2027. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the electoral system must change before a credible vote and that Washington had secured Rodríguez’s assurance weeks ago that Machado could return safely. Machado’s spokesperson said any meeting with Rodríguez or other officials would be transparent and follow an agenda. The European Union called for inclusive, Venezuelan-led dialogue toward free and fair elections; no election date has been announced.
world.image_alt: Machado offers talks as U.S. outlines route to Venezuelan elections

world.title: Reports say Netanyahu pressed for Iran action before Israeli election
world.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pressed for military action against Iran in the weeks before Tuesday’s election and, after encountering resistance, for a separate step short of an overt strike, according to Israeli defense officials cited by The New York Times. Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, chief of staff of the Israe
world.content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pressed for military action against Iran in the weeks before Tuesday’s election and, after encountering resistance, for a separate step short of an overt strike, according to Israeli defense officials cited by The New York Times. Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF), warned that Iran could misread the move and retaliate, risking renewed conflict. Netanyahu’s office and Defense Minister Israel Katz denied a rift or a plan to initiate an attack before the vote. Katz said Israel would respond forcefully if Iran attacked first; the IDF said it based its decisions on security and professional considerations. The White House said the United States would not attack Iran before its Nov. 3 midterm elections. Israel is holding its first national election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of putting political interests above national security, while Netanyahu has portrayed the Iran threat as central to the country’s future. Israelis vote on Oct. 27.
world.image_alt: Reports say Netanyahu pressed for Iran action before Israeli election

world.title: Serbia’s student movement faces government talks after election victory
world.summary: Serbia’s Student List, a movement-backed slate of candidates, is preparing to form a government after defeating former President Aleksandar Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party in Sunday’s parliamentary election. Preliminary projections put the Student List at about 53% of the vote and 141 seats in the 250-member parliame
world.content: Serbia’s Student List, a movement-backed slate of candidates, is preparing to form a government after defeating former President Aleksandar Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party in Sunday’s parliamentary election. Preliminary projections put the Student List at about 53% of the vote and 141 seats in the 250-member parliament, giving it a majority without coalition partners. The movement has no single leader, and its candidates have little governing experience. Its platform promises action against corruption and changes to public institutions, but the candidates have not named a prime minister or cabinet. Analysts warn that bureaucratic resistance and difficulty maintaining internal unity could complicate the transition. Once parliament convenes after final results are announced, the constitution allows 90 days to form a government. The candidates also face a year-end budget deadline as public and private debt rise. The movement’s foreign-policy positions are not fully settled: its platform calls for a referendum on EU accession while pledging to maintain ties with Russia and oppose sanctions against Moscow.
world.image_alt: Serbia’s student movement faces government talks after election victory

world.title: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials open Iran talks to avert renewed war
world.summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Oct. 26, in the first joint high-level visit by the three signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement since its formation in August. Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Field Marshal Asim Muni
world.content: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Oct. 26, in the first joint high-level visit by the three signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement since its formation in August. Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin were among the delegates who met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei. The talks aimed to reduce the risk of renewed fighting after President Trump said Washington might strike Iran again and Israel warned of possible attacks. The officials also discussed Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and the wider conflict’s effects on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The four governments agreed to continue discussions on regional peace and security but announced no specific deal or date for another meeting. Israel holds its election on Oct. 27, followed by the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.
world.image_alt: Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials open Iran talks to avert renewed war

world.title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church attack kills nine in Karak
world.summary: Jordan’s air force struck targets in southern Syria on Monday, Oct. 26, saying the sites belonged to militant groups linked to the gunmen who killed nine people at a church in Jordan three days earlier. The Jordanian military said its strikes destroyed positions and vehicles and killed or wounded members of the groups;
world.content: Jordan’s air force struck targets in southern Syria on Monday, Oct. 26, saying the sites belonged to militant groups linked to the gunmen who killed nine people at a church in Jordan three days earlier. The Jordanian military said its strikes destroyed positions and vehicles and killed or wounded members of the groups; it did not identify the groups or give precise locations. Syrian authorities said the strikes killed between five and eight civilians, including children, and that Jordan had not coordinated the operation in advance. Jordan said it had coordinated with Damascus. Syria’s government opened an investigation and said it was communicating with Jordan about the incident. The strikes followed a shooting during a funeral at St. George’s Greek Orthodox Church in Hammoud, in Karak governorate, on Oct. 23. Jordanian security forces arrested three Jordanian suspects after a shootout on Monday; all three suspects were wounded. Syria closed the Nassib crossing on Tuesday, suspending passenger and commercial traffic in both directions.
world.image_alt: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church attack kills nine in Karak

business.title: U.S. Halloween candy sales fall as prices squeeze shoppers
business.summary: U.S. Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 from a year earlier as shoppers faced high chocolate prices and pressure from other household costs. The decline followed an 11.7% drop in mid-September, while U.S. Halloween spending was forecast to reach a record $13.5 billion this year, including $4.1
business.content: U.S. Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% in the month ending Oct. 17 from a year earlier as shoppers faced high chocolate prices and pressure from other household costs. The decline followed an 11.7% drop in mid-September, while U.S. Halloween spending was forecast to reach a record $13.5 billion this year, including $4.1 billion on candy. Cocoa prices have eased from their 2025 peak but began rising again in spring as the Iran war disrupted African fertilizer supplies. Hot, dry conditions are also expected to weigh on production through February. The National Confectioners Association said the peak selling period was just beginning and expressed confidence in consumer enthusiasm.
business.image_alt: U.S. Halloween candy sales fall as prices squeeze shoppers

business.title: U.S. gasoline average under Trump edges past Biden-era level
business.summary: Americans have paid an average of $3.472 per gallon for regular gasoline during President Donald Trump’s second term, narrowly above the $3.471 average under former President Joe Biden, according to American Automobile Association data reported by Reuters. The figures are not adjusted for inflation. Diesel has averaged
business.content: Americans have paid an average of $3.472 per gallon for regular gasoline during President Donald Trump’s second term, narrowly above the $3.471 average under former President Joe Biden, according to American Automobile Association data reported by Reuters. The figures are not adjusted for inflation. Diesel has averaged $4.343 a gallon under Trump, versus $4.078 under Biden, and reached a record $6.523 on Sept. 22. Fuel supplies tightened after the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in February, disrupting crude flows around the Strait of Hormuz and adding to pressure from Russia’s war in Ukraine. The White House says Middle East oil exports have recovered above prewar levels, but fuel costs remain high. It expects prices to fall when the conflict ends. Republicans are defending narrow majorities in Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
business.image_alt: U.S. gasoline average under Trump edges past Biden-era level

business.title: Apple offers replacements after screen faults hit first foldable iPhone
business.summary: Apple said it will replace a small number of iPhone Duo foldable phones after owners reported cracks, bright lines and other inner-screen failures days after the device went on sale. The company has not disclosed how many units are affected or identified a cause. It told users with display problems to contact AppleCare
business.content: Apple said it will replace a small number of iPhone Duo foldable phones after owners reported cracks, bright lines and other inner-screen failures days after the device went on sale. The company has not disclosed how many units are affected or identified a cause. It told users with display problems to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The Duo is Apple’s first foldable iPhone; rivals have sold folding phones for years. Some online images may be fake, and analysts said the reports so far were too limited to establish how widespread the fault is. Repair firm iFixit suggested the hinge could be involved, but Apple has not confirmed that theory.
business.image_alt: Apple offers replacements after screen faults hit first foldable iPhone

business.title: Sterling slips ahead of UK budget as traders weigh rate decisions
business.summary: Sterling fell on Monday as investors reduced positions ahead of Wednesday’s UK budget and a week of central bank decisions. The pound fell 0.31% to 83.98 pence per euro and 0.15% to $1.3348. The euro recovered after Moody’s left France’s credit rating unchanged, easing concerns that France’s fiscal problems could spill
business.content: Sterling fell on Monday as investors reduced positions ahead of Wednesday’s UK budget and a week of central bank decisions. The pound fell 0.31% to 83.98 pence per euro and 0.15% to $1.3348. The euro recovered after Moody’s left France’s credit rating unchanged, easing concerns that France’s fiscal problems could spill over into euro-zone assets. Markets expect the UK finance minister to prioritize bond-market stability. Easing concerns about UK debt and resilient economic data have supported sterling recently. The European Central Bank is widely expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday, although most economists polled by Reuters expect a quarter-point increase in December.
business.image_alt: Sterling slips ahead of UK budget as traders weigh rate decisions

business.title: JetBlue posts $257 million quarterly loss as fuel costs surge
business.summary: JetBlue Airways reported a $257 million net loss for the third quarter, compared with a $143 million loss a year earlier, as its fuel bill climbed 61% to $868 million. Average fares rose more than 19% to $245.11, and revenue reached $2.81 billion, just below analysts’ $2.82 billion estimate. The airline’s shares closed
business.content: JetBlue Airways reported a $257 million net loss for the third quarter, compared with a $143 million loss a year earlier, as its fuel bill climbed 61% to $868 million. Average fares rose more than 19% to $245.11, and revenue reached $2.81 billion, just below analysts’ $2.82 billion estimate. The airline’s shares closed down nearly 10% Monday at a record low before rising about 11% in after-hours trading. The New York-based carrier is cutting costs and seeking more premium revenue as it tries to return to sustained profitability. JetBlue ended September with $2.2 billion in liquidity and $8.4 billion in debt; executives were scheduled to discuss the results with analysts Tuesday, Oct. 27.
business.image_alt: JetBlue posts $257 million quarterly loss as fuel costs surge

business.title: Rising U.S. prices put Republicans at risk in November midterms
business.summary: With U.S. midterm elections a week away, persistent inflation and higher household costs are putting Republicans on the defensive as voters judge President Donald Trump’s economic record. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the year through last month, compared with 3% when Trump took office; voters have also faced higher f
business.content: With U.S. midterm elections a week away, persistent inflation and higher household costs are putting Republicans on the defensive as voters judge President Donald Trump’s economic record. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the year through last month, compared with 3% when Trump took office; voters have also faced higher fuel costs and mortgage rates. Trump has dismissed affordability concerns as a Democratic “con job” and said oil prices will fall when the Iran war ends. Voters and analysts have pointed to the war and Trump’s tariffs as factors adding to costs. An Urban Institute analysis estimates that 49% of families cannot afford basic living costs, while a survey of small businesses found that nearly two-thirds of owners had recently cut or skipped their own pay to keep their businesses operating. The midterm elections are next week.
business.image_alt: Rising U.S. prices put Republicans at risk in November midterms

business.title: China’s industrial profits jump 14.4% as technology gains widen
business.summary: Profits at China’s major industrial firms rose 14.4% in September from a year earlier, accelerating from 4.2% growth in August as technology-related manufacturing and higher producer prices supported earnings. The increase was the strongest since June, while cumulative profits rose 15.5% in January-September, slightly
business.content: Profits at China’s major industrial firms rose 14.4% in September from a year earlier, accelerating from 4.2% growth in August as technology-related manufacturing and higher producer prices supported earnings. The increase was the strongest since June, while cumulative profits rose 15.5% in January-September, slightly below the 15.7% gain through August. The gains were concentrated in industries tied to artificial intelligence, electronics and digital infrastructure, while weak household demand continued to weigh on businesses serving consumers. Higher energy and raw-material costs also lifted factory-gate prices, adding pressure on downstream manufacturers facing weak domestic demand. China’s economy grew 4.5% in the third quarter, compared with the government’s 4.5%-5% full-year target. Consumer spending remained soft, with September retail sales rising 1.1%.
business.image_alt: China’s industrial profits jump 14.4% as technology gains widen

business.title: Meta launches $95 billion stock raise to finance AI infrastructure
business.summary: Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, said on Oct. 26 it plans to raise up to $95 billion through stock sales to finance artificial-intelligence infrastructure and develop what it calls personal superintelligence. The plan begins with about $35 billion in public offerings—$22.5 billion
business.content: Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, said on Oct. 26 it plans to raise up to $95 billion through stock sales to finance artificial-intelligence infrastructure and develop what it calls personal superintelligence. The plan begins with about $35 billion in public offerings—$22.5 billion of Class A common stock and $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred shares—followed by a separate at-the-market sale of up to $60 billion in new, non-voting Class C shares. Meta reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, its first negative free cash flow in more than a decade, and raised its 2026 capital-expenditure forecast to $135 billion-$145 billion. The company says it will also use operating cash flow, investment-grade debt and partnerships to fund its spending. Its latest quarterly filing showed $82.45 billion in cash and marketable securities and $80.92 billion in long-term debt as of Sept. 30. Meta expects the Class C sale to begin after those shares start trading in the first quarter of 2027; the company has not finalized the timing or terms of that $60 billion program. Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom have expressed interest in buying up to $5 billion of the initial Class A offering.
business.image_alt: Meta launches $95 billion stock raise to finance AI infrastructure

science.title: Australian jumping spider study identifies two sleep stages, including REM-like phase
science.summary: Researchers at the University of Bonn, led by behavioral ecologists Nadja Geiger and Daniela C. Rößler, found that the Australian jumping spider Portia fimbriata has two distinct sleep stages, one marked by eye movements and muscle twitches resembling rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. The study, published in Proceedings
science.content: Researchers at the University of Bonn, led by behavioral ecologists Nadja Geiger and Daniela C. Rößler, found that the Australian jumping spider Portia fimbriata has two distinct sleep stages, one marked by eye movements and muscle twitches resembling rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. The study, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, provides the first comprehensive behavioral confirmation of sleep in a spider. The spiders became less responsive to sound during both quiet and REM-like periods and compensated for disrupted rest by spending more time in REM-like behavior. The findings rely on behavioral tests and video, not direct measurements of brain activity, so they do not establish that spider sleep works like human sleep. Researchers plan to compare sleep in wild and laboratory spiders and investigate what happens in arachnid brains during sleep.
science.image_alt: Australian jumping spider study identifies two sleep stages, including REM-like phase

science.title: U.S. and India target 2029 for expanded space capabilities
science.summary: The U.S. Space Force is urging companies to prepare satellites and software for cislunar missions, seeking commercial systems ready for launch by 2029. India’s space agency separately aims to have four operational launch pads by that year. Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy, the Space Force’s portfolio acquisition executive for a
science.content: The U.S. Space Force is urging companies to prepare satellites and software for cislunar missions, seeking commercial systems ready for launch by 2029. India’s space agency separately aims to have four operational launch pads by that year. Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy, the Space Force’s portfolio acquisition executive for advanced programs, said the U.S. push reflects changing Pentagon priorities and is partly linked to China’s lunar plans. Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) Chairman V. Narayanan said private-sector partnerships will help meet demand for satellite launches, while the agency will remain public. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said docking exercises with SpaceX and Blue Origin lunar landers are expected next year. NASA plans to wait as long as possible before choosing a lander for Artemis IV, scheduled for 2028.
science.image_alt: U.S. and India target 2029 for expanded space capabilities

science.title: Researchers warn automated AI development could accelerate capability gains
science.summary: A paper on the arXiv research preprint repository, revised Oct. 26, examines whether automating artificial intelligence research and development could trigger an “intelligence explosion,” compressing years of advances into months or less. Its 22 authors say AI systems already write most of the code inside the companies
science.content: A paper on the arXiv research preprint repository, revised Oct. 26, examines whether automating artificial intelligence research and development could trigger an “intelligence explosion,” compressing years of advances into months or less. Its 22 authors say AI systems already write most of the code inside the companies building them. The authors describe the evidence as preliminary but say AI could automate most AI research work within a few years and possibly all of it. They warn that rapid acceleration could outpace society’s ability to respond, increase the risk of losing control over superhuman systems and weaken checks on power. The paper calls for policymakers to improve visibility into automated AI research and develop ways to steer or constrain it. In its proposed stock-market listing, Anthropic says it expects at least $518 billion in cloud and infrastructure spending over the next decade, much of it locked into non-cancellable contracts.
science.image_alt: Researchers warn automated AI development could accelerate capability gains

science.title: Mathematicians debate who must verify OpenAI
science.summary: Mathematicians face the work of checking and explaining AI-generated proofs as difficult research problems increasingly serve as benchmarks for AI models, said Terence Tao, a mathematics professor at UCLA. Tao said some outputs are poorly polished and fail to explain the reasoning or what researchers should pursue next
science.content: Mathematicians face the work of checking and explaining AI-generated proofs as difficult research problems increasingly serve as benchmarks for AI models, said Terence Tao, a mathematics professor at UCLA. Tao said some outputs are poorly polished and fail to explain the reasoning or what researchers should pursue next. He also warned that access to powerful AI could change who can do leading-edge mathematics. OpenAI says its models generated new results in mathematics, computer science and physics. The company released the mathematics and computer science materials for examination, while a selected group of physicists is preparing its account before publication. Mathematician Alex Iosevich called the mathematics result a historic development but said he felt sadness about changes in the field.
science.image_alt: Mathematicians debate who must verify OpenAI

science.title: NASA ends Swift telescope mission after failed $30 million rescue
science.summary: NASA has ended the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory’s science mission after the space telescope’s orbit fell too low for reliable observations and a private attempt to raise it failed. Swift made its final scientific observation on Oct. 20 and is expected to reenter Earth’s atmosphere in the coming weeks. NASA says most
science.content: NASA has ended the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory’s science mission after the space telescope’s orbit fell too low for reliable observations and a private attempt to raise it failed. Swift made its final scientific observation on Oct. 20 and is expected to reenter Earth’s atmosphere in the coming weeks. NASA says most of the spacecraft will burn up, though some debris could survive. Launched in November 2004 for a planned two-year mission, Swift spent nearly 22 years tracking gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic events. Arizona-based Katalyst Space’s LINK spacecraft was intended to capture the observatory and boost its orbit, but propulsion and attitude-control problems prevented the rescue. Swift recorded more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and observed more than 1,400 supernovae; its data have contributed to about 7,000 scientific papers. NASA is considering how to sustain rapid-response observations with existing telescopes and future missions.
science.image_alt: NASA ends Swift telescope mission after failed $30 million rescue

science.title: Extra schooling under UK reform linked to fewer dementia diagnoses
science.summary: A study of more than 100,000 UK Biobank participants found that a 1972 British law requiring teenagers to stay in school until 16 was associated with fewer diagnoses of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias nearly 50 years later. Using the reform’s September 1, 1957, birth-date cutoff, researchers compared people s
science.content: A study of more than 100,000 UK Biobank participants found that a 1972 British law requiring teenagers to stay in school until 16 was associated with fewer diagnoses of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias nearly 50 years later. Using the reform’s September 1, 1957, birth-date cutoff, researchers compared people subject to different school-leaving rules and reported a 0.88% reduction in dementia incidence among those affected. Researchers also found the reduction among participants with high genetic susceptibility. They cautioned that dementia was uncommon in this cohort, whose diagnoses were tracked only through age 65, making the estimate imprecise. Continued follow-up will help determine whether the difference persists as participants age.
science.image_alt: Extra schooling under UK reform linked to fewer dementia diagnoses

science.title: Antarctic grass and pearlwort show opposite responses to experimental warming
science.summary: A seven-year field experiment on King George Island found that Antarctica’s only two native flowering plants responded in opposite ways to warming: Antarctic hair grass showed reduced water flow through its leaves and lower photosynthesis, while Antarctic pearlwort showed increases in both. The findings come from plant
science.content: A seven-year field experiment on King George Island found that Antarctica’s only two native flowering plants responded in opposite ways to warming: Antarctic hair grass showed reduced water flow through its leaves and lower photosynthesis, while Antarctic pearlwort showed increases in both. The findings come from plants grown in open-top chambers near Poland’s Henryk Arctowski Antarctic Station. The chambers produced sharp temperature swings, not just higher average temperatures: during the 2018–19 summer, plants inside spent far more time below freezing than those outside. Researchers are now examining plants that have remained in the chambers for 16 years, along with microorganisms living around them.
science.image_alt: Antarctic grass and pearlwort show opposite responses to experimental warming

science.title: Animal blood colors reflect distinct oxygen-carrying proteins and adaptations
science.summary: Animal blood can be blue, violet, green or white because species use different oxygen-transport proteins or pigments, according to a Knowable Magazine feature republished by Nautilus and ZME Science. Octopuses, squid and crustaceans use copper-containing hemocyanin. Some marine worms and brachiopods use purple hemeryth
science.content: Animal blood can be blue, violet, green or white because species use different oxygen-transport proteins or pigments, according to a Knowable Magazine feature republished by Nautilus and ZME Science. Octopuses, squid and crustaceans use copper-containing hemocyanin. Some marine worms and brachiopods use purple hemerythrin, while New Guinea lizards accumulate green biliverdin. Antarctic blackfin icefish lack hemoglobin and red blood cells, relying instead on oxygen dissolved in their blood and enlarged hearts and capillaries. Vampire bats are the only known mammals that live exclusively on blood; specialized kidneys and gut microbes help them handle the diet.
science.image_alt: Animal blood colors reflect distinct oxygen-carrying proteins and adaptations

sports.title: Patriots coach Vrabel objects to leaked $250,000 NFL fine
sports.summary: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday he would not discuss a reported $250,000 NFL fine for his conduct toward officials, saying the matter was supposed to remain confidential. The league reportedly put the fine on hold and could waive it if Vrabel demonstrates good behavior. The fine followed a Week
sports.content: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday he would not discuss a reported $250,000 NFL fine for his conduct toward officials, saying the matter was supposed to remain confidential. The league reportedly put the fine on hold and could waive it if Vrabel demonstrates good behavior. The fine followed a Week 4 game against the Buffalo Bills, when Vrabel received an unsportsmanlike-conduct penalty for swearing at an official over a holding call. He later apologized and said he needed to handle those moments better. Asked how he would speak to officials in the future, Vrabel joked that he would praise their calls. He also said officials do a difficult job and that coaches’ responses to mistakes matter.
sports.image_alt: Patriots coach Vrabel objects to leaked $250,000 NFL fine

sports.title: Cowboys beat Eagles 38-21 as Dallas revives running game
sports.summary: The Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night, closing NFL Week 7 with season highs of 204 rushing yards and 38 points. Javonte Williams led Dallas with a career-best 155 rushing yards, and Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes as the Cowboys moved within one game of the New York Giants in t
sports.content: The Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night, closing NFL Week 7 with season highs of 204 rushing yards and 38 points. Javonte Williams led Dallas with a career-best 155 rushing yards, and Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes as the Cowboys moved within one game of the New York Giants in the NFC East. The loss extended Philadelphia’s losing streak to five games, while the Giants’ 27-21 overtime win over Houston left them atop the division at 4-2-1. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the regular season. Dallas’s offense had its most productive game of the season, though CBS Sports said the Cowboys’ defense needed to improve.

sports.title: Zverev can claim world No. 1 with Vienna quarterfinal run

sports.content: Alexander Zverev can become the world’s top-ranked men’s player for the first time by reaching the quarterfinals at the Erste Bank Open in Vienna, where he opens against Spanish wild card Martin Landaluce. The German trails rankings leader Jannik Sinner by 100 points, and a quarterfinal berth would be enough to overtake him. Sinner is not defending points at the Vienna event. Zverev’s first-round match is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27. Carlos Alcaraz, the third-ranked player, is also competing in Vienna after missing more than four months earlier this season with a wrist injury. He says he needs match play to regain his rhythm. He has already qualified for the ATP Finals and is seeking a fourth tour-level title this season. Alcaraz meets Karen Khachanov in his opener.

sports.content: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and chose to bowl in the third Twenty20 international against New Zealand in Wellington on Tuesday, with the visitors leading the five-match series 2-0. New Zealand were 94 for two after nine overs. Finn Allen scored 40 before Nitish Kumar Reddy dismissed him, while Daryl Mitchell was unbeaten on 40. India can secure the series with a win after taking the first two matches by four wickets each. They chased 226 in the opener, then reached a target of 181 in Christchurch as Tilak Varma and Nitish Reddy shared an unbeaten stand of 69 from 30 balls. India kept the same XI. New Zealand made three changes to their pace attack, with Matt Henry out for the rest of the series and Lockie Ferguson missing this match. The fourth match is scheduled for Auckland on October 30, followed by the final game in Hamilton on November 1.

sports.content: The WNBA has moved Finals Game 6 between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries to 12:30 p.m. Eastern on Thursday, Oct. 29, at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena. Golden State leads the series 3-2 after a 64-55 win in Game 5. The weekday matinee replaces the originally planned 8 p.m. start, putting tipoff at 9:30 a.m. in California, where the Valkyries are based. The change keeps the Finals at the 17,000-seat arena rather than the Dream’s regular 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena and accommodates the Atlanta Hawks’ scheduled game against the Cleveland Cavaliers that evening. The Hawks moved their tipoff back an hour to 8 p.m. Eastern. The WNBA and NBA explored alternatives, including moving Game 6 to Friday and a possible Game 7 to Nov. 3, but chose the Thursday matinee. Game 6 will air on USA Network and stream on Peacock. If Atlanta wins, the deciding Game 7 is scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 31, at San Francisco’s Chase Center.

sports.title: Cowboys beat Eagles 38-21 as Javonte Williams rushes for 155 yards
sports.summary: The Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 in Philadelphia on Monday, ending a two-game skid and handing the Eagles their fifth straight loss. Dallas running back Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown, while quarterback Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns, includi
sports.content: The Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 in Philadelphia on Monday, ending a two-game skid and handing the Eagles their fifth straight loss. Dallas running back Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown, while quarterback Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns, including two to CeeDee Lamb. Philadelphia briefly led 21-20 late in the third quarter after backup quarterback Tanner McKee threw a touchdown pass to rookie receiver Makai Lemon. Prescott answered with a touchdown pass to Lamb and a two-point conversion as Dallas scored the game’s final 18 points. The Cowboys improved to 3-4, and the Eagles fell to 2-5. The New York Giants lead the NFC East at 4-2-1. Running back Saquon Barkley returned after missing more than two games with a hamstring injury, scored on an eight-yard run and gained 62 yards on seven carries. He was later listed as questionable to return with a back injury. Philadelphia also played without receiver DeVonta Smith and starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs.

sports.title: Graeme McDowell exits LIV as 2027 relaunch struggles to retain stars

sports.content: Graeme McDowell, the 2010 U.S. Open champion, has ruled out joining LIV Golf’s planned 2027 relaunch, becoming the latest prominent player to leave the breakaway league. He said he was grateful for his four years with LIV and looked forward to the next stage of his career. He has previously discussed returning to the DP World Tour, where he has won 11 times. LIV is trying to rebuild after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) ended its financial backing and the league entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. Private equity firm BC Partners Credit has proposed up to $300 million in financing, but the league reportedly needs 30 to 40 players for the new circuit. About 15 had expressed interest, and just five had publicly said they wanted to stay. LIV extended its deadline for player commitments to October 30, when the PIF can begin winding down the business. A bankruptcy court hearing is scheduled for November 6.

sports.content: Oklahoma City Thunder forward Jalen Williams will undergo surgery for a fractured left fibula and dislocated ankle, while guard Cason Wallace needs surgery for a torn labrum in his left shoulder. Both were injured in Sunday’s 108-101 win over the Los Angeles Clippers. General manager Sam Presti said the team will set return timelines after the operations. Both players could miss most or all of the 2026-27 season, but the Thunder have not ruled either out for the season. The injuries sideline two starters for the defending champions: Williams is an All-Star and All-NBA player, while Wallace earned All-Defensive honors last season. The Thunder beat the Phoenix Suns 125-114 on Monday, with Ajay Mitchell scoring a career-high 30 points. Guard Alex Caruso sprained his right ankle and left the game. Oklahoma City will reassess its roster options after the injured players undergo surgery and the team has more information about their recovery timelines.
